title: Advantage Weighted Matching: Aligning RL with Pretraining in Diffusion Models
claim: Matching the pretraining objective with a clean target lowers variance and reaches high quality far faster than the standard RL baseline.
layout: 3 panels: large top convergence plot, bottom-left formulation diagrams, bottom-right variance illustration
description: The top panel (a) is a large line plot of GenEval score against training GPU hours. An orange AWM curve shoots up almost vertically to about 0.985. A blue Flow-GRPO curve climbs slowly to about 0.94. Dashed horizontal lines mark the GPT-4o (0.84) and SD3.5-Medium (0.63) baselines. A red dashed arrow and bold red text mark a 16.54x speedup. Bottom-left panel (b) shows two vertical chains of boxes from x1 to x0. DDPO uses an x_t to x_s DDPM step with the objective max log p(x_s|x_t)·A(x0). AWM goes from x0 back to x_t by adding noise, with the objective max log p(x0)·A(x0). Bottom-right panel (c) compares noisy and clean targets using noise and image thumbnails of a red chair, with a sad High Variance label for DDPO and a happy Low Variance label for AWM.
caption: AWM reduces variance and speeds up RL. (a) Convergence: On GenEval, AWM reaches the same quality with 8× fewer GPU hours than Flow-GRPO. (b) Formulations: DDPO optimizes per-step Gaussian likelihood on xt−1, whereas AWM applies advantage-weighted score/flow matching on x0. (c) Target variance: DSM with noisy target xs (DDPO implicitly doing) has higher variance than DSM with clean x0 (AWM).
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a central paradigm for advancing Large Language Models (LLMs), where both pre-training and RL post-training stages are grounded in the same log-likelihood formulation. In contrast, recent RL approaches for diffusion models, most notably Denoising Diffusion Policy Optimization (DDPO), optimize an objective different from the pretraining objectives--score/flow matching loss. In this work, we establish a novel theoretical analysis: DDPO is an implicit form of score/flow matching with noisy targets, which increases variance and slows convergence. Building on this analysis, we introduce Advantage Weighted Matching (AWM), a policy-gradient method for diffusion. It uses the score/flow-matching loss and reweights each sample by its advantage. In effect, AWM raises the influence of high-reward samples and suppresses low-reward ones while keeping the modeling objective identical to pretraining. This simple yet effective design yields substantial benefits: on the GenEval, OCR, and PickScore benchmarks, AWM delivers up to a $34\times$ speedup over Flow-GRPO (which builds on DDPO), when applied to Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and FLUX, without compromising generation quality. Code is available at https://github.com/scxue/advantage_weighted_matching
